notes: Variant assumption is a prone/lying hamstring curl machine with pad resistance at the lower leg and motion occurring primarily through knee flexion. Primary roles are intentionally limited to biceps femoris, semitendinosus, and semimembranosus. Biceps femoris and semitendinosus have direct EMG support from lying/prone leg-curl studies; semimembranosus is backed primarily by Maeo et al.'s MRI training data rather than isolated surface EMG. Gastrocnemius is included as a secondary role because Marchetti et al. directly measured gastrocnemius lateralis during prone leg-curl knee-flexion contractions; it is not treated as a main target. No support muscles were added because hip, pelvis, trunk, and grip stabilization claims were not backed strongly enough for a visible role. Main unresolved uncertainties are commercial machine geometry, prone bench hip angle, roller placement, cam/resistance curve, unilateral versus bilateral setup, ankle position, and whether users compare this entry with seated leg curls, which train the biarticular hamstrings at longer muscle lengths. The shared anatomy file now includes local BodyParts3D mappings for biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus, and gastrocnemius.
